rules.text: Do not flag the rough, fibrous texture of the cap (hilum) or its jagged edge as a defect.
rules.justification: The agent incorrectly identified the natural, coarse texture and irregular boundary of the hazelnut cap as a surface defect. This is a standard morphological feature of the class.

rules.text: Flag circular, semi-transparent light spots or 'ghost' marks on wood grain as anomalies, even if they appear faint or lack sharp edges.
rules.justification: The agent missed faint, circular light spots (likely oil or water stains) because they lacked the high contrast or sharp boundaries of typical defects. The rule extends detection to include these subtle, translucent surface variations.

rules.text: Flag rim chips or cracks even if they appear as small, localized bright reflections or irregularities on the edge.
rules.justification: The agent missed a clear chip on the rim, likely dismissing it due to its small size or confusing the bright reflection from the broken edge with a normal specular highlight.

rules.text: Do not flag bright, metallic specular highlights on copper strands as defects.
rules.justification: The agent misclassified the natural high-reflectivity of the copper conductor surface as a defect. The bright spots are consistent with the material properties of copper under inspection lighting.

rules.text: Flag thin, linear foreign fibers or scratches that contrast with the woven texture, even if small.
rules.justification: The agent missed a distinct stray fiber/scratch in the center. The error stems from under-weighting small, high-contrast linear defects against complex textures.

rules.text: Do not flag natural metal grain texture or slight surface unevenness on the shank as a defect.
rules.justification: The agent misidentified the inherent rough texture of the metal surface on the screw shank as a structural defect, failing to distinguish between material grain and actual damage.

rules.text: Do not flag minor asymmetry or roughness in the drive slot of the screw head as a defect.
rules.justification: The agent incorrectly classified the standard manufacturing imperfections found in the screw head's drive slot as a defect, ignoring that these are typical for this class.

rules.text: Flag as anomaly if bristles are splayed, bent, or disheveled, deviating from the uniform, upright alignment of the reference set.
rules.justification: The agent failed to classify the obvious splaying and dishevelment of the bristles as a defect, likely due to a narrow definition of 'surface defect' that excluded structural deformation of the bristles themselves.

rules.text: Flag items with localized edge chipping or irregularities on the outer perimeter of the cross-arms.
rules.justification: The agent missed a specific structural defect (edge chip) on the arm, focusing only on general texture. It failed to distinguish between manufacturing texture and physical damage.

rules.text: Do not flag consistent, fine-grained surface texture or machining marks on the arms as defects.
rules.justification: The agent incorrectly identified standard manufacturing texture (grain) as a defect. This texture is a normal characteristic of the metal_nut class.

rules.text: Flag distinct translucent or semi-transparent shards/fragments resting on the surface, even if they appear ghostly or low-contrast against the background.
rules.justification: The agent failed to detect a clear foreign object (shard) because its translucency reduced visual contrast against the speckled tile background, leading to a false negative.

rules.text: Flag dark, localized stains or discolorations on the fabric adjacent to the zipper teeth as defects.
rules.justification: The agent focused on the zipper structure and missed the distinct dark stain on the fabric, which is a clear surface defect.

rules.text: Flag thin, dark linear intrusions that cross the mesh pattern diagonally, even if they are subtle or blend with the background texture.
rules.justification: The agent missed a distinct diagonal dark line (likely a wire or scratch) because it was thin and overlaid on the complex mesh texture. The rule emphasizes detecting linear foreign objects regardless of their subtlety.

rules.text: Do not flag global variations in mesh orientation, density, or lighting gradients if the underlying expanded metal structure remains consistent with reference patterns.
rules.justification: The agent falsely flagged a normal image due to perceived 'pattern rotation' or 'density variation'. These are likely natural variations in the manufacturing or imaging process, not structural defects.

rules.text: Do not flag scattered red speckles on white tablets as defects if the 'FF' imprint is clear and the tablet shape is intact.
rules.justification: The agent incorrectly flagged these normal pills because it misinterpreted the inherent red speckle texture as a surface defect, failing to recognize it as a standard feature of this specific pill class.

rules.text: Flag as anomaly if the black capsule half shows surface unevenness, texture variation, or coating defects compared to the smooth orange half.
rules.justification: The agent missed anomalies on the black half of the capsule, specifically texture variations and coating unevenness, likely due to low contrast or assuming the black color masks defects.

rules.text: Do not flag as anomaly if the 'actavis' logo is present on the black half, even if the text appears slightly faint or low-contrast.
rules.justification: The agent incorrectly flagged normal capsules as anomalies, likely misinterpreting the standard low-contrast white-on-black logo as a defect or missing text.
